title: Tables Are References, Not Copies
summary: Assigning or passing a table shares the SAME table: `local b = a` makes two names for one table. Mutations through either name are visible everywhere. Copy explicitly when you need independence.

explanation.whatItIs: Tables are handles to shared storage, not the storage itself. Two variables can point at one table; changes 'through one door' appear 'in the other room'.
explanation.whyItExists: Efficiency — big tables shouldn't duplicate on assignment; sharing is a feature until it's a bug.
symptoms: Default-config tables mutating after first player tweaks them
explanation.fix: Copy deliberately: shallow copy for flat tables ({table.unpack(t)} or a loop), deep copy function for nested ones. Or freeze shared constants.
tips: table.freeze(DEFAULTS) makes accidental mutation error loudly
Immutability discipline: treat shared configs as read-only
commonMistakes: local defaults = masterConfig; defaults.hp = 50 — you just edited masterConfig
Shallow copy and assuming nested tables are independent

examples.title: Reference vs copy
examples.code:
local stats = { hp = 100, mp = 50 }

local alias = stats            -- same table!
alias.hp = 1
print(stats.hp)                --> 1  (surprise if you expected 100)

-- Shallow copy:
local copy = table.clone(stats)
copy.hp = 200
print(stats.hp)                --> 1 (untouched by copy)

-- Nested caveat:
local deep = { pos = { x = 0, y = 0 } }
local shallow = table.clone(deep)
shallow.pos.x = 9
print(deep.pos.x)              --> 9  (nested table still shared!)
